records.subagent_summary: My 8 public rollouts scored 2/8 (execution 149.97); all six failures enumerated the divisor pairs of the public number but never fed Sasha's announcement back as a constraint on Masha's candidate partners, so they collapsed to a single reading, declared "the partner is uniquely determined, contradiction", and emitted an unjustified divisor (143 three times, 11 once) while two burned the token cap looping on that contradiction. The revision keeps the two-candidates-per-private-value counting rule but adds the missing mechanism explicitly: turn the earlier announcement into a set of admissible partner values and re-count each later speaker's candidates only within that set.

All 8 round-5 rollouts scored 1, so training is saturated and the loss is transfer plus wasted tokens. The dominant failure was the incumbent's compressed modulus line: rollouts wrote |z-a|^n = |c|^(1/n)|z-b|^n (mixing the power and the root in one step) and then carried a wrong ratio for thousands of tokens before self-correcting, with the two longest rollouts (12.2k and 7.0k tokens, 37 and 35 hedges) spending most of their length on that constant. A second sink is that the incumbent gives only a procedure for the circle, so rollouts re-derived the midpoint/half-distance from scratch or ran a full x+iy completion of the square as well; the revision splits the modulus into two explicit steps and supplies closed-form center and radius so the circle step is a substitution.

Round-5 training with the incumbent fell to 4/8, and all four failures share one root cause: the invariance check is run as two independently guessed sample orientations, so a botched rotated-case value (one rollout got a single-point overlap and answered 5, another got a whole-shape overlap, a third got a value disagreeing with the aligned case) either ends the rollout wrong or triggers an open-ended piecewise search that ran out the 16384-token budget in three of eight. Winners instead trusted the aligned computation and argued invariance directly. This revision replaces sample-and-compare with an explicit one-line rotation-symmetry proof (rotating by 2*pi/k maps S to itself and permutes the k wedge positions, partitioning S into k equal pieces) plus a hard floor rejecting single-point and full-containment overlaps, so the student never needs a second computed orientation to commit.

My 8 public rollouts scored 5/8 and, unlike earlier rounds, all three failures terminated normally with wrong answers rather than truncating. Two derived a correct per-function root bound but then reported that cap as the final count instead of summing over the N functions, and one of those used the interpolation count deg P + 1 rather than the root count deg P; the third never used the root bound and assumed each function contributes exactly one index. The revision therefore fixes the cap to the root count and adds an explicit aggregation step plus reject-rules for the two observed off-by-a-factor endings.

All 8 public rollouts were correct (train_i=1.0), so train is saturated and only transfer binds; heldout has tracked hint length inversely across rounds (73 tok -> 0.15, 151 -> 0.1375, 161 -> 0.125, 189 -> 0.075), so this revision is shorter than the 151-token incumbent. The three longest correct rollouts thrashed on hundreds of midpoint/vertex-sum lines and contradiction talk after adding a redundant second closure condition, while the short clean rollouts carried one on-curve parameter; historical failures on this hint instead assigned the translated vertex a y from the carried shift rather than from f, got a point off the graph, and reported an area anyway. The hint keeps only the portable pipeline plus those two cheap guards and drops the narrow discriminant-flip and exponential-form verbosity.

My 8 public rollouts scored 0/8 in two clusters: four asserted the delivery order is deterministically reversed, and three assumed uniformity (one answer per permutation, or per which item lands last); one exhausted its token budget on unstructured enumeration. Rounds 1-4 showed that longer enumerate-the-tree hints all cost held-out relative to the 83-token incumbent, so this revision stays short and swaps the abstract state-graph advice for one portable structural fact: an output order corresponds to a unique legal push/pop word, which simultaneously refutes the forced-outcome and equiprobable-permutation fallacies and reduces the task to pricing that word by its free-versus-forced moves.

All 8 rollouts scored 0 (7 hit the 16384-token cap): every one reinterpreted the rows as a polynomial in the condition number rather than the node, producing a degree-2005 polynomial with only 2004 roots, then spent the budget resolving the phantom free root and reported 1/2005, 0, or a harmonic sum. Two rollouts built a small analogue but gave it more conditions than unknowns, so the toy came out inconsistent and they abandoned the correct framing. This revision keeps the incumbent's proven functional opening and adds the two missing mechanical steps: absorb one node power into each weight so the annihilated exponents start at degree 0 (which is why the functional reads off a top coefficient), and scale the toy's condition count with its unknown count.

5/8 public rollouts were correct; all three failures shared one mode, and it was not arithmetic: they read the stated number of equal groups as the unit count, divided every listed total by it, saw each quotient come out whole, and treated that successful divisibility check as confirmation, so they never ran the gcd/maximum-admissible-count step at all. The incumbent already warns that group wording only imposes a multiple constraint, but it sits mid-paragraph after the gcd sentence and was missed. I front-loaded that warning and added the portable closing of the loophole, namely that divisibility is necessary but not sufficient because every divisor of the gcd also passes, so one must continue to the maximum.

All 8 public rollouts were correct again (8/8, 4.4k-6.0k tokens, none truncated), so the training question stays saturated and every remaining point is transfer; the one visible waste is that some rollouts burned ~3k tokens looping on the algebra of AB^n=BA^n (repeatedly mis-cancelling before recovering B=+-A) and others accepted B=-A purely on the hint's authority. Across rounds only the round-2 proposal raised heldout (0.175), and its distinctive ingredient was the factored condition AB(A^(n-1)-B^(n-1))=0 with an instruction to carry both branches and let data eliminate one, while its train loss came from abstracting the trigger and dropping the fixed-point/verify steps. This revision therefore keeps the incumbent's concrete p(q)=q(p) trigger, centered ansatz, and verification spine untouched and swaps only the asserted odd-n sign for that factored both-branch derivation, so unseen problems whose data favours the B=A branch are not forced into a sign flip.

Only 2/8 correct and six of six failures hit the token cap; all six produced a smallest-size count that contradicted their own larger-size count and then looped for thousands of tokens re-deriving it. Tracing the block swaps shows the shared root cause is refilling a swapped block from the original letters instead of the state the previous sub-step produced, which silently undoes an earlier sub-step and makes the operation look like an involution. The revision therefore states the rigid-unit rule with CURRENT contents, adds a came-from-the-previous-line check, and tells the student to commit once one larger size confirms the closed form instead of restarting.
